CHIEF COMPLAINT
Nonhealing foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male with a two-month history of a foot ulcer. The ulcer recently became red and started draining, which prompted the patient's visit. The patient reports the injury occurred from walking barefoot on Dewey Beach. Patient describes intermittent throbbing sensation in the foot but denies severe localized pain; his primary concern is the redness and drainage. Patient saw his primary care physician who prescribed antibiotics, but the patient has not yet picked them up from the pharmacy and cannot recall the specific medication name, though he states he has taken it before. Patient has diabetes and reports taking his medication but does not regularly check his blood sugar. Patient states his last A1C was around 10.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports intermittent throbbing in the foot. Vital signs are normal with no fever. On examination, patient reports increased pressure sensation at the wound site but denies distinct pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus, poorly controlled.

MEDICATIONS
Diabetes medication (specific agent not specified). Antibiotics prescribed by PCP but not yet obtained.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in an ambulance. Patient was injured while walking barefoot on Dewey Beach.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, no fever. Right foot examination reveals a 1 x 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. Wound has redness, drainage, and surrounding edema. No necrosis, no odor, and no bony exposure noted. Patient experiences increased pressure sensation on palpation but no distinct pain.

RESULTS
X-ray of right foot shows no evidence of osteomyelitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diabetic foot ulcer with infection. Plan includes ordering ankle brachial index (ABI) to assess blood supply to the foot. Will perform debridement to remove dead tissue. Will prescribe clindamycin 400 mg orally twice daily for 7 days to treat infection. Will provide surgical shoe to reduce pressure on foot for one month. Follow-up appointment scheduled for two weeks, at which time reassessment and possible repeat debridement will be performed. Patient instructed to call office with any concerns or if fever develops or if black discoloration appears; patient should go to urgent care or emergency room if emergent symptoms develop.
